requirement_vague: Verify multiple comments can be added to the same article with unique IDs

implementation.code_reference:
class Comment(SQLModel, table=True):
    id: Optional[int] = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)
...
comment = Comment(body=body, created_at=ts, updated_at=ts, author_id=current_user.id, article_id=article.id)
...
comments = sorted(article.comments, key=lambda c: c.id or 0)
return {"comments": [comment_dict(c, viewer, session) for c in comments]}
implementation.reasoning: The code allows creating multiple Comment rows for the same article because each new comment is inserted with the same article_id and no uniqueness constraint prevents multiple comments per article. Each comment gets a database primary-key id, and GET /api/articles/{slug}/comments returns all persisted comments with their id and body, so three added comments would be returned with distinct ids and preserved bodies.
